newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close mixed in heavy turnover.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close mixed in heavy turnover.

text.p: * Toronto stocks ended mixed after trading in a narrow range, pulled down by sagging pipelines and golds. * Vacations reduce players. * 88.03 million shares traded worth C$1.42 million.
Toronto stocks ended mixed on Tuesday, with the focus on dropping pipelines and golds after the market gained nearly 300 points so far in August.

"This is a momentum that cannot be maintained, so this market is giving back some of its gains," said P and C Holdings President Ron Meisels. "I think it'll take a few more days before it sells off enough" for investors to return, hunting for bargains.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index lost 12.8 points to close at 5173.9 points. However, advancing issues edged out declining ones 444 to 438.
Since July 30, the key 300 index has climbed from 4891 points to today's close of 5173, gaining 282 points.
Market players have been decimated by vacations ahead of a long holiday weekend, Meisels said. Canadian markets will be closed on Monday, September 2, for Labor Day.
All of Toronto's 14 sub-indices fell except for conglomerates and retail issues. Pipelines, golds, transports and forestry products lost the most ground.

National Bank of Canada rose 0.10 to 11.90 in turnover of 2.5 million shares. Today Canada's third and fourth largest banks, the Bank of Montreal and the Bank of Nova Scotia, kicked off the reporting period for financial institutions by posting better-than-anticipated third quarter profits.

* Rogers Communications Inc was also active. The nation's largest cable-television firm saw shares slip 0.05 to 9.20 on 2.4 million shares, continuing Monday's fall. Chief financial officer Graham Savage resigned yesterday, the second senior executive to jump ship this year.
